title: Tuberculosis contact evaluation completion: a Lean redesign of the contact pathway
subtitle: Value stream mapping and flow redesign from case notification to completed evaluation
statement: Only 71 percent of about 1,300 contacts of pulmonary tuberculosis cases completed evaluation within 60 days in 2025, against a provincial target of 90 percent. Completion was lowest for shift-working household contacts, contacts in shelters and contacts needing an interpreter. The pathway has many handoffs between nurses, clinics, the central office and the hospital, and contacts are lost at each. The program wants to map the value stream and redesign the flow.
whoAffected: Contacts of about 110 people with pulmonary tuberculosis a year, especially people in shelters, shift workers and people who need interpreters; TB nurses, clinic staff and the central office.
whatHurts: A contact with infection who is never evaluated can develop active disease and transmit it; delays mean repeated calls, lost samples and anxious families.
currentPractice: Case nurse lists contacts, a second nurse phones them, blood is drawn at three clinics, results go to the central office by fax or courier, and positives are booked for hospital chest X-ray.
whyNow: A completion rate far below target, approval for two mapping days and a monthly data extract newly approved.
patientCenteredGoal: Every contact is evaluated quickly and conveniently, whatever their housing, working hours or language.
summary: Problem framed as a Lean redesign of a multi-handoff public health pathway.
